items.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
items.snippet: Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

items.title: What an ancient volcanic eruption teaches us about resilience today
items.snippet: When a massive environmental disaster strikes, do societies simply collapse and disappear? Or do people find a way to adapt, rebuild and recover?

items.title: Noise-cancelling headphones prevent vomiting after surgery
items.snippet: Nausea and vomiting are common after surgery, which may be partly related to the noises patients are exposed to, even under general anaesthetic. Wearing noise-cancelling headphones while on the operating table reduces the risk

items.title: 25 Oct = 25 years since: Windows XP, one of the most popular and widely used versions of the Microsoft Windows operating system, was released for retail sale.
items.snippet: Windows XP is a major release of Microsoft's Windows NT operating system. It was released to manufacturing on August 24, 2001, and later to retail on October 25 that year. It is a direct successor to Windows 2000 for high-end and business users and Windows Me for home users.

items.title: 01 Nov = 70 years since: The Indian states Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka were formally created under the States Reorganisation Act.
items.snippet: Kerala, officially Keralam, is a state on the Malabar Coast of southern India. It was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, which unified the country's Malayalam-speaking regions into a single state.
